page: Microsoft Azure M16bds_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz. The instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a 410 GB SSD, and the instance supports Premium Storage configurations.

Benchmark evaluations place the M16bds_v3 in the top 25% tier for single-threaded gzip compression at 32.97 GB/sec and Geekbench single-core processing with a score of 2196.0. Text processing performance is also strong, registering 2785.0 in Geekbench. Multi-core performance metrics, such as the stress-ng multi-core score of 16883.26 and the Geekbench multi-core score of 13388.0, fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests yield 107.61 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 68.03 GB/sec for large-block write operations. For small language model workloads, the instance achieves a strong text generation speed of 303.34 tokens/sec on a 135M parameter model, while prompt processing for a medium 7B model averages 99.68 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the M16bds_v3 offers a balanced allocation of high-frequency Intel Xeon processing power and a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads without the premium cost of ultra-high memory tiers. The inclusion of a 410 GB local SSD and block storage capabilities supports data-heavy applications. This hardware profile is suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems such as Redis, software compilation, and text-processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure M16bds_v3 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine from the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8473C processor running at 4.0 GHz, paired with 128.0 GB of RAM and a 410 GB local SSD. The instance delivers strong single-core performance, scoring in the top 25% for Geekbench single-core (2196.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (32.97 GB/sec). Multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics, such as a stress-ng multi-core score of 16883.26 and a large-block read bandwidth of 107.61 GB/sec, align with mid-range industry averages. Lacking a dedicated GPU, the server utilizes Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) to support CPU-based inference, achieving 303.34 tokens/sec for small model text generation. This configuration is suited for database operations, memory-intensive caching, text processing, and software compilation.
